newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's May mined gold output falls 5.26 percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru's May mined gold output falls 5.26 percent.

text.p: Peru's gold output fell 5.26 percent to 5.090 tonnes in May compared with the same month last year, according to preliminary figures released Tuesday by the Energy and Mines Ministry.
Gold output rose 5.42 percent overall to 27.68 tonnes in the first five months, compared with the same period last year, the ministry added in its monthly report.
Peru's gold production in 1996 rose 12.2 percent to 64.8 tonnes from 57.7 tonnes.

Peru is Latin America's second largest gold producer after Brazil and the 12th largest in the world. The country's largest gold producer is Minera Yanacocha S.A., a joint venture operated by Newmont Mining Co.
The ministry's figures include estimates for output by Peru's informal gold miners, who account for about 40 percent of national output.
